answer: Spectral admission pricing. Each agent action must reference a live coordination thread; the protocol charges a fee equal to the harmonic sum over distinct threads an identity touches per epoch, so spreading across N threads costs log N more than staying in one. A haven of idle capacity is priced at zero, making dormancy free but breadth expensive. Attackers pay superlinear costs to fan out sybils, while honest agents cluster cheaply. The fable is that volume equals commitment—the mechanism inverts it.
